objections.raw_quote: Before we go too deep, because I have done a virtual trainer, I found it successful, it's been a few years, probably, I ended probably about five years ago, but I want to know what the payment structure, and I know that may range or not, but before we spend too much time on this call, just out of respect to each other's time.
objections.rep_response: Attempted to reverse it — 'Is that because you have like a small budget for yourself? ... what is sort of your budget looking like?' — and when the prospect refused to anchor, disclosed a range: a community tier at a couple of hundred a month, and one-to-one 'at least into the four figures, usually ranging between two and six'. The prospect then named $200-300 a month and the rep conceded the main offer was out of reach within four minutes of the call starting.

Counter-evidence toward a future close: 'I'm good with it conceptually', he liked the video form-feedback mechanism specifically, he has bought virtual coaching before and rated it, and he pays a muscle activation therapist monthly.

Counter-evidence against: he anchored himself at $200-300 a month before hearing anything, the rep conceded four minutes in that four figures was 'quite out of what you would want to spend', and an unresolved objection to text-only coaching was left standing at the end of the call.

notable.note: Two things a principal should take from a twenty-minute call. First, this is the fullest price disclosure anywhere in the batch and it does not match the stated offer: three months $4,000, six months $6,000, twelve months $9,000, community $200 a month or $2,000 a year — plus, earlier in the same call, a spoken range of 'between $2,000 and $6,000 to $8,000'. The three-month $4,000 tier and the $8,000 top end appear nowhere in the stated offer. Second, the rep revealed in passing that the pre-call nurture sequence is sent by an automated persona: 'I don't know if you've already seen the video that Sophia, the bot, sent to you.' The prospect had watched or skipped five of those videos already and had not been told they were automated. Clinically, the prospect has a chronic lower back that locks up nightly and is under the care of a muscle activation therapist twice a month; no one asked whether that clinician had cleared loaded kettlebell training, and the rep suggested the programme would remove his need to stretch in the morning. The rep also mentioned working until 3am as routine.
